newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians take to streets to protest road deaths.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians take to streets to protest road deaths.

text.p: Thousands of Brazilians took to the streets on Sunday to protest "savage traffic" that claims more than 50,000 lives every year.
Police said up to 5,000 people protested in the capital Brasilia and national CBN radio said several thousand more joined a march in Rio de Janeiro.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, writing in the Correio Braziliense newspaper, said the 50,000 road deaths registered in Brazil every year was a cause for shame.
"It's well past the time to put an end to this massacre," he said.
Families took over one of the main thoroughfares of Brasilia, a city of 1.8 million people where some 500 people have been killed this year in road accidents.
Bands played samba music while speakers called on drivers to respect speed limits and red lights in the futuristic city designed for cars and notoriously unfriendly to pedestrians.

Correio said 679 people died last year in 77,698 accidents in Rio de Janeiro -- regarded as one of the most perilous places to drive in Brazil because of recklessness and fear among drivers that stopping at red lights makes them easy targets for car-jackers.
Cardoso said he supported a bill currently being considered by Congress which would criminalize dangerous driving resulting in death. He said it was time careless driving was considered a crime.

"We are already paying too high a price, in lives and suffering, for our tolerance of bad drivers," he wrote. "The suffering inflicted is neither less nor more unavoidable just because the weapon used to kill is a car, and not a revolver."
